newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb settles state probes.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb settles state probes.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb said on Tuesday that it has reached a settlement with 17 state attorneys general who, over the last three years, have investigated the company's former contact lens marketing practices.
Those practices were discontinued by the eye care company in 1995, the company said in a statement.

Bausch & Lomb, while maintaining that the old practice was legitimate, has agreed to limits on its future contact lens marketing practices and will pay $1.7 million, or $100,000 per state, to cover state costs.
Bausch & Lomb said existing litigation reserves are adequate to cover the settlement expenses.

The investigation, which began in September 1994, involved the states' claim that Bausch & Lomb failed to disclose to consumers that certain differently named lenses, which were intended for different prescribed replacement schedules, were identical.

In 1995, Bausch & Lomb voluntarily added the OptimaFW name to the Medalist and SeeQuence2 packaging to ensure that there is no question that each of the different replacement systems uses the same lens design, it said.

Neither the settlement nor the labeling change in any way implies or acknowledges any wrongdoing by Bausch & Lomb, the company said. At no time did the states take legal action against the company, it said.
